report.summary: The change replaces the owner-only guard requireProject with requireReadableProject in withOwnedRepository. All 13 issue, comment and label handlers use that guard, so any user can now list, read, create, update and delete issues, comments and labels on another user's public Artifacts project. This contradicts 09 Git Forge (owned project required), 11 Public Profile P3 (issues stay owner-only for every project; visitors refused for issues of a public project) and the 04 UI make-public notice ('Issues, pull requests and checks stay private'). No spec change comes with it.

findings.text: The issue, comment and label guard now lets any user through for any public project, including all mutations (create, update, delete of issues, comments and labels). Spec 09 and 11 require project ownership for every project.

evidence.quote: const project = await requireReadableProject(ctx.env, ctx.user, projectId);
evidence.why: requireReadableProject (common.ts:83) throws only when `!row || (row.userId !== viewer?.id && row.visibility !== "public")`. For a project with visibility 'public', a user whose id is not the owner passes, and then e.g. deleteRepositoryIssue / createRepositoryLabel run against the owner's project. The spec says otherwise: 09 Git Forge line 77 says issue functions 'require an owned Artifacts project'; 11 Public Profile P3 says 'Issues, pull requests, checks, conversations and workspaces stay owner-only for every project'; 04 UI line 305 tells the owner 'Issues, pull requests and checks stay private.' The previous requireProject filtered on eq(schema.projects.userId, userId). No spec tab is changed in this diff (CLAUDE.md rule 16).

checked.risk: Security: ownership and visibility checks on issue, comment and label handlers
Spec conformance for issue access and public projects
Failure paths: NOT_FOUND / VALIDATION_FAILED / INTERNAL mapping in withOwnedRepository unchanged
Tests: whether any test covers visitor refusal for public-project issues
